title_ru: Сад на крыше кормит целый район
description_ru: Вымышленная новость о жителях дома, которые вырастили овощи на крыше и делятся урожаем.
text:
Residents of an apartment building in the city of Eastham have turned their grey rooftop into a thriving vegetable garden. The project, called Green Roof, began last year with only six wooden boxes and a few bags of soil.

Today the garden has more than sixty boxes, a small greenhouse and even three beehives. Volunteers have grown tomatoes, carrots, beans and herbs, and they give away everything that they cannot eat themselves. Last month alone, the group delivered two hundred kilograms of fresh vegetables to a nearby food bank.

The idea came from retired nurse Dorothy Cole, who is seventy-two years old. "I used to have a big garden in the countryside," she said. "When I moved here, I missed the smell of the earth. One day I looked up at the empty roof and thought, why not?"

At first, the building's owner refused to give permission. He was worried that the weight of the soil might damage the roof. Engineers checked the structure and confirmed that it was safe, so he changed his mind.

The garden has also changed life inside the building. Neighbours who had never spoken now meet every Saturday to water the plants and share tea. "Before the garden, I did not know anyone's name," said student Ahmed Rahman. "Now I know everybody on all eight floors."

City officials have visited the roof and say they would like to help other buildings do the same. If the plan goes ahead, similar gardens could appear across Eastham by next summer.

questions.question: What happens to the extra vegetables?
questions.answer: They are given to a food bank.

questions.question: Why did the owner first refuse permission?
questions.answer: He worried the soil was too heavy for the roof.
